name: OpenStack Tacker
what_it_is: Tacker is an OpenStack-based NFV Orchestrator service with a built-in general-purpose VNF Manager for deploying and operating Virtual Network Functions (VNFs). It follows the ETSI MANO Architectural Framework and delivers end-to-end orchestration for VNFs on OpenStack and Kubernetes VIMs.
components: tacker-horizon (Horizon UI plugin for web-based management)
protocols: OpenStack REST APIs (Keystone, Nova, Neutron, Heat)
measurement: No built-in metrics collection or observability tooling documented in README or devstack guide
configuration: TACKER_MODE variable: omit for all-in-one, set to standalone for minimal deployment
Database backend: MySQL (default) or PostgreSQL (requires bytea_output = 'escape')
Branch selection: master (latest) or stable/2024.2 (pinned release)
local.conf template files for devstack setup
Optional Kubernetes VIM support via devstack-plugin-container
modes: all-in-one: full Devstack + Tacker on a single machine (default)
standalone: Tacker + mandatory OpenStack services only, used in CI (Zuul) environments
constraints: Minimum hardware: 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, 80 GB storage
Ubuntu LTS only; DevStack supports only the two latest Ubuntu LTS releases
Kubernetes VIM support limited to Ubuntu hosts only
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml found in the repository (404 on master branch)
No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering capabilities documented
No native metrics/monitoring — relies on external OpenStack telemetry services
No explicit performance benchmarking or load-testing tooling
